cases.title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
cases.bench: 13 Judges (S.M. Sikri C.J., J.M. Shelat, K.S. Hegde, A.N. Grover, A.N. Ray, P.J. Reddy, D.G. Palekar, H.R. Khanna, K.K. Mathew, M.H. Beg, S.N. Dwivedi, A.K. Mukherjea, Y.V. Chandrachud JJ.)
cases.material_facts: The religious head of Edneer Mutt challenged the Kerala Land Reforms Amendment Acts of 1969 and 1971 and the 24th, 25th, and 29th Constitutional Amendments.
cases.constitutional_questions: Whether Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 is unlimited and whether fundamental rights can be abrogated.
cases.holding_and_ratio: Parliament has wide power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 but cannot alter the Basic Structure or framework of the Constitution.
cases.dissents_and_concurrences: 7:6 majority (Khanna J. holding the decisive vote on basic structure). Dissent by Ray, Palekar, Mathew, Beg, Dwivedi, Chandrachud JJ.
cases.subsequent_treatment: Followed in Indira Gandhi (1975), Minerva Mills (1980), Waman Rao (1981), S.R. Bommai (1994), I.R. Coelho (2007). Good law.
cases.legislative_evolution_relationship: DIRECT_LEGISLATIVE_RESPONSE: 42nd Amendment attempted to nullify basic structure (Art 368(4)-(5)), which was subsequently struck down in Minerva Mills.

cases.title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
cases.bench: 7 Judges (M.H. Beg C.J., Y.V. Chandrachud, P.N. Bhagwati, V.R. Krishna Iyer, N.L. Untwalia, S. Murtaza Fazal Ali, P.S. Kailasam JJ.)
cases.material_facts: Petitioner's passport was impounded by the passport authorities under Section 10(3)(c) of the Passports Act in public interest without assigning reasons.
cases.constitutional_questions: Whether Section 10(3)(c) violates Articles 14, 19, and 21, and whether 'procedure established by law' requires natural justice.
cases.holding_and_ratio: Articles 14, 19, and 21 form a golden triangle; procedure under Article 21 must be fair, just, and reasonable, not arbitrary.
cases.dissents_and_concurrences: Unanimous on expanding Article 21 to incorporate substantive fairness.
cases.subsequent_treatment: Overruled A.K. Gopalan (1950); followed in hundreds of subsequent human rights and criminal justice decisions. Good law.
cases.legislative_evolution_relationship: DOCTRINAL_INTERACTION: Prompted administrative guidelines for passport impoundment and natural justice hearing procedures.

cases.title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
cases.bench: 9 Judges (J.S. Khehar C.J., J. Chelameswar, S.A. Bobde, R.K. Agrawal, R.F. Nariman, A.M. Sapre, D.Y. Chandrachud, S.K. Kaul, S. Abdul Nazeer JJ.)
cases.material_facts: Challenge to biometric data collection under the Aadhaar scheme leading to reference on whether privacy is a fundamental right.
cases.constitutional_questions: Whether the Constitution of India recognizes a fundamental right to privacy.
cases.holding_and_ratio: The right to privacy is a fundamental right protected under Articles 14, 19, and 21 and intrinsic to human dignity and autonomy.
cases.dissents_and_concurrences: Unanimous 9:0 decision declaring privacy a fundamental right. Expressly overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and ADM Jabalpur (1976).
cases.subsequent_treatment: Applied in Navtej Johar (2018), Joseph Shine (2018), Anuradha Bhasin (2020), Pegasus (2021). Good law.
cases.legislative_evolution_relationship: DIRECT_LEGISLATIVE_RESPONSE: Srikrishna Committee Report and enactment of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

cases.title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.material_facts: Arrest of citizens for posting political opinions on Facebook under Section 66A of the Information Technology Act 2000.
cases.constitutional_questions: Whether Section 66A of the IT Act violates freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a).
cases.holding_and_ratio: Section 66A is unconstitutional, vague, and overbroad, failing the reasonable restrictions test of Article 19(2).
cases.subsequent_treatment: Followed nationwide; Section 66A remains dead letter. Good law.
cases.legislative_evolution_relationship: JUDICIAL_INVALIDATION: Struck down Section 66A in its entirety.

cases.title: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
cases.bench: 5 Judges (Dipak Misra C.J., R.F. Nariman, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra JJ.)
cases.material_facts: Constitutional challenge to Section 377 IPC criminalizing consensual sexual acts between adults of same sex.
cases.constitutional_questions: Whether Section 377 IPC violates Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(a), and 21.
cases.holding_and_ratio: Section 377 read down to exclude consensual adult sexual intimacy in private. Suresh Koushal (2014) overruled.
cases.dissents_and_concurrences: Unanimous 5:0 bench with concurring opinions by Misra CJ, Nariman J, Chandrachud J, Malhotra J.
cases.legislative_evolution_relationship: DOCTRINAL_INTERACTION: Section 377 modified in judicial operation; BNS 2023 Section 63/64 restructures sexual offences.
